title: Agribusiness and irrigation in the Paranapanema basin (Southwest São Paulo)
text: Status: Completed · Period: 2024–2025 · Team: Cepea (coordination: Geraldo Barros, Nicole Castro, Mauro Osaki), with support from ASPIPP

title: Agribusiness and irrigation in the Paranapanema basin (Southwest São Paulo)
text:
About the project
The Upper Paranapanema basin, in the southwest of the state of São Paulo, is a major producer of grains and horticultural crops and one of the largest irrigated areas in the state. It is also one of the regions with the lowest income and human development indicators in São Paulo. In partnership with the Southwest São Paulo Association of Irrigators and No-Till Farmers (ASPIPP), Cepea measured how much agribusiness contributes to income and jobs in the region and how much of that comes from irrigated agriculture. The reference year is 2021.

title: Agribusiness and irrigation in the Paranapanema basin (Southwest São Paulo)
text:
Objective
Measure the GDP and employment generated by agribusiness in 42 municipalities of the Upper Paranapanema basin, covering inputs, primary production, agroindustry, and services, and estimate the contribution of irrigated agriculture to regional GDP.

title: Agribusiness and irrigation in the Paranapanema basin (Southwest São Paulo)
text:
Main results

In 2021, agribusiness generated R$ 14.8 billion in GDP and 191 thousand jobs in the region.
Agribusiness accounted for 38.4% of regional GDP and 50.4% of regional employment, well above the state average, where agribusiness represented 18.2% of GDP.
The region’s primary sector represented 13.3% of São Paulo’s agricultural and livestock production, although the region accounts for only 1.4% of the state’s total GDP.
About 23% of the region’s cropland is irrigated, which corresponds to 36% of the irrigated area in the state.
Irrigated agriculture generated at least R$ 1.37 billion in GDP, equal to 9% of regional agribusiness GDP and 4% of the region’s total GDP.

title: Corn ethanol for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) in the United States
text:
About the study
The long-run outlook for corn ethanol is uncertain as the vehicle fleet shifts toward electric and hybrid cars. Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), a key component of the U.S. plan to reach net-zero aviation emissions by 2050, could open a new market for ethanol, but its size depends on policy choices such as how the carbon intensity of ethanol-based SAF is measured and whether it qualifies for tax credits.

title: Corn ethanol for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) in the United States

Quantify the market and welfare effects of using corn ethanol to produce sustainable aviation fuel in the United States.

title: Brazilian agribusiness (Cepea)
text:
About the project
Cepea, at the University of São Paulo, publishes regular indicators that track the performance of Brazilian agribusiness. Agribusiness is measured as the sum of four segments: agricultural inputs, primary production, agroindustry, and agribusiness services.

title: Brazilian agribusiness (Cepea)
text:
Objective
Provide timely, consistent measures of the size and performance of Brazilian agribusiness for researchers, policymakers, and the private sector.

title: Brazilian agribusiness (Cepea)
text:
My role

Calculate and monitor the agribusiness GDP and labor market indicators, and write the quarterly analytical reports.
Contribute to the calculation of the agricultural Producer Price Index (IPPA).

title: Brazilian agribusiness (Cepea)
text:
Methods

GDP: measured for each of the four agribusiness segments, with real income (GDP-income) as the main indicator, which combines changes in volume and in relative prices.
Labor market: based on microdata from the IBGE Continuous National Household Sample Survey (PNAD-C), using Cepea’s method to identify agribusiness activities.

title: How much does it cost to reduce emissions in Nebraska? Evidence from corn and soybean production
text:
About the study
Crop production in Nebraska is a major source of agricultural greenhouse gas emissions, and producers may soon face incentives to lower the carbon intensity of their corn and soybeans. This dissertation chapter studies what it would cost them to do so.

title: Carbon intensity of Nebraska feedstuffs
text: Status: Completed · Period: 2023–2026 · Team: Felipe Almeida, Richard Perrin, Lilyan Fulginiti, Elliott Dennis

title: Carbon intensity of Nebraska feedstuffs
text:
About the study
New U.S. clean-fuel tax credits reward biofuels according to their carbon intensity (CI), the greenhouse gas emissions per unit of output over the production life cycle. Because feedstock emissions are a large part of fuel CI, ethanol plants and beef producers may start paying premiums for low-CI grain and feed. This project estimates the CI that Nebraska producers can expect for their crops and for the co-products fed to beef cattle.

title: Carbon intensity of Nebraska feedstuffs
text:
Objective
Estimate the expected life-cycle CI of corn and soybeans produced in Nebraska, by region and irrigation, and extend those estimates to distillers grains with solubles (DGS) and soybean meal (SBM).

title: Carbon intensity of Nebraska feedstuffs
text:
Methods

Two life-cycle assessment models: GREET FD-CIC (U.S. Department of Energy) and IFSM (U.S. Department of Agriculture).
Three Nebraska regions (West, Central, East), each with irrigated and rainfed production.
Value-based allocation of emissions between co-products (ethanol and DGS; soybean oil and SBM).

title: Carbon intensity of Nebraska feedstuffs
text:
Main results

Corn: expected CI of 0.29 (IFSM) and 0.25 (GREET) lb CO₂e per lb of grain dry matter, close to the U.S. default of 0.297.
Soybeans: expected CI of 0.28 (IFSM) and 0.32 (GREET), compared with a U.S. default of 0.338.
Irrigation: irrigated corn and soybeans have roughly 10% lower CI than rainfed crops.
Distillers grains: drying raises CI. Modified DGS is about 23% higher than wet DGS, and dry DGS is about 50% higher (weighted averages of 0.20–0.23 for wet, 0.25–0.28 for modified, and 0.31–0.33 for dry DGS).
Soybean meal: expected CI of 0.36 (IFSM) and 0.38 (GREET) kg CO₂e per kg of dry matter.

title: GDP and labor market of São Paulo agribusiness
text: Status: Completed · Period: 2024–2026 · Team: Cepea (coordination: Geraldo Barros, Nicole Castro, Felipe Almeida), with support from FIESP

title: GDP and labor market of São Paulo agribusiness
text:
About the project
São Paulo is Brazil’s largest state economy and accounts for about a quarter of Brazilian agribusiness GDP. In partnership with the Federation of Industries of the State of São Paulo (FIESP), Cepea built GDP and labor market indicators for São Paulo agribusiness, applying the same methods used for the national indicators. I co-coordinated the project.

title: GDP and labor market of São Paulo agribusiness
text:
Objective
Measure the size and performance of São Paulo agribusiness, covering GDP since 2010 and employment from 2012 to 2024, and identify the drivers of its recent evolution.

title: GDP and labor market of São Paulo agribusiness
text:
Main results
GDP (2024)

Agribusiness GDP reached R$ 657.6 billion in 2024, up 3.96% from 2023.
Growth came from prices (+7.1% in relative prices), while volume fell 2.93%, mainly because of crop losses.
São Paulo agribusiness represented 24.0% of Brazilian agribusiness GDP, 18.9% of São Paulo GDP, and 5.6% of Brazil’s GDP.
By segment: inputs −3.76%, primary production −11.36%, agroindustry +6.89%, and services +7.83%.

Labor market (2012–2024)

Agribusiness employed 4.34 million people in 2024, 17.2% of total employment in the state and 15.3% of Brazilian agribusiness employment.
Agribusiness employment grew 4.6% between 2012 and 2024, against 18.9% for the state as a whole, so the sector lost share as an employer.
In 2024, 54.7% of workers had a formal employment contract, 75.3% had completed at least high school, and 60.1% were men.
Labor productivity fell over the period, because employment grew faster than output.
